features.description: Pre-impl sufficiency auditor module at `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/sufficiency_auditor.py`. Pure text-only auditor (no MCP, no runtime evidence). Function shape: `run_sufficiency_audit(plan_dir: Path) -> list[SufficiencyFinding]`. Reads `plan.md` frontmatter (gets `goal_type` + `links.objective_contract`); loads the objective contract file via the path reference; loads `features.json`; constructs a sufficiency prompt walking objective_contract.user_journeys against features.json acceptance criteria; resolves the auditor agent via `agent_manifest` per Goal Governance V1 §5 vendor policy (D006 — cross-vendor required by default; no hardcoded vendor); writes findings to `evidence/goal-governance/pre_impl/sufficiency-findings.json` (matches F0's evidence path convention). Tests cover: finding-extraction logic with mocked agent response; unknown goal_type handling; missing objective_contract handling; malformed contract handling; agent_manifest vendor resolution. Direct path (D008).
steps: Pre-flight: confirm F002 close-out at expected SHA. Confirm 997 passed, 6 skipped baseline still holds.

Define `SufficiencyFinding` Pydantic model in `sufficiency_auditor.py`: `severity: str` (validated against the audit envelope severity enum — reuse the validation pattern from F0's `GoalGapFinding`); `journey_id: str` (which user journey from objective_contract); `gap_class: str` (high-level taxonomy: `coverage_gap`, `missing_feature`, `wiring_gap`, `parity_gap`, `integration_gap`); `description: str` (≥40 chars — substantive, not stubs); `feature_refs: list[str]` (which existing features in features.json are related, or empty if no current feature covers this); `recommendation: str | None`.

Define helper `_load_objective_contract(plan_dir: Path) -> ObjectiveContract`: reads plan.md frontmatter, extracts `links.objective_contract`, resolves path relative to plan_dir, loads + validates against `ObjectiveContract` model from claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/models/objective_contract_model.py. Raises clear errors on each failure mode (missing goal_type, missing links field, file doesn't exist, malformed contents).

Define helper `_resolve_goal_auditor_agent(implementer_agent: str | None) -> str`: reads `agent_manifest`, returns the configured goal_auditor agent. Per D006: cross-vendor required by default; raises `ValueError` if same-vendor and no operator override is recorded. Today's expected default when implementer is Claude: Codex. Resolution path documented + tested; never hardcoded.

Define `_build_sufficiency_prompt(contract: ObjectiveContract, features: list[Feature]) -> str`: constructs the auditor prompt with structured sections — objective contract summary, user journeys list, current features list, instruction to surface gaps as structured JSON output. Prompt is the load-bearing piece; it must explicitly direct the auditor toward the gap classes that matter (coverage matrix, integration concerns, parity gaps, journey completeness) per Goal Governance V1 §3.1.

Define `_parse_sufficiency_response(response: str) -> list[SufficiencyFinding]`: parses the auditor's JSON output into structured findings; validates each via Pydantic; raises clear errors on malformed responses.

Define `run_sufficiency_audit(plan_dir: Path, implementer_agent: str | None = None) -> list[SufficiencyFinding]`: top-level entry point. Loads contract + features, resolves agent, dispatches the auditor, parses response, writes `evidence/goal-governance/pre_impl/sufficiency-findings.json` per F0's path convention, returns findings. Pure text-only — no MCP, no runtime evidence.

features.description: Plan-lock sufficiency gate/check. Wires F003's `run_sufficiency_audit()` into **every plan-lock path**, not just CLI draft → active flip (D011). Lock paths to gate: (a) CLI `dontpanic plan lock <plan-dir>`; (b) plan-validator at next validation run if status was edited manually; (c) MCP server programmatic lock paths. Gate behavior: if `goal_type ∉ {parity, new_feature, migration, incident}`, no sufficiency check, lock proceeds normally; if gated, run `run_sufficiency_audit()` — refuse the lock if any finding has severity ≥ blocking severity, with a structured error pointing at the findings file. Operator override: `--ignore-sufficiency-findings <reason>` flag (text reason required, recorded in evidence). Override is human-in-the-loop; no auto-override. Direct path (D008).

Define helper `_should_gate_sufficiency(plan_data: Plan) -> bool`: returns True iff `plan_data.goal_type in {parity, new_feature, migration, incident}`. Pure function.

Define `enforce_sufficiency_gate(plan_dir: Path, override_reason: str | None = None) -> None`: top-level gate function. (a) Loads plan.md frontmatter; (b) if `_should_gate_sufficiency()` returns False, returns silently (no-op for non-gated plans); (c) otherwise runs `run_sufficiency_audit()`; (d) checks findings — if any has severity ≥ blocking AND no override_reason supplied, raises `SufficiencyGateError` with a structured message pointing at the findings file; (e) if override_reason supplied, writes the override to `evidence/goal-governance/pre_impl/override.json` recording timestamp, reason, operator (if available from environment), and the bypassed findings. Returns silently on pass.
Wire `enforce_sufficiency_gate()` into all identified lock paths from step 2. CLI gets a new `--ignore-sufficiency-findings <reason>` flag that translates to the override_reason argument.
